answer: A nebula of small agents can resist sybils when each identity must forge itself through a chain of useful, verifiable micro-tasks: a newborn sparrow identity earns only tiny quotas after completing real work whose results peers re-check, and each completed task raises the next task's difficulty slightly. Creating a thousand fake identities means building a thousand separate work chains, each costing real compute and wall-clock time, while one honest agent's chain compounds into trusted standing that cannot be copied or transferred.
